family.description: This group of families is one of several protein families that are always found associated with prokaryotic CRISPRs, themselves a family of clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats, DNA repeats found in nearly half of all bacterial and archaeal genomes. These DNA repeat regions have a remarkably regular structure: unique sequences of constant size, called spacers, sit between each pair of repeats [[cite:PUB00020781]]. It has been shown that the CRISPRs are virus-derived sequences acquired by the host to enable them to resist viral infection. The Cas proteins from the host use the CRISPRs to mediate an antiviral response. After transcription of the CRISPR, a complex of Cas proteins termed Cascade cleaves a CRISPR RNA precursor in each repeat and retains the cleavage products containing the virus-derived sequence. Assisted by the helicase Cas3, these mature CRISPR RNAs then serve as small guide RNAs that enable Cascade to interfere with virus proliferation [[cite:PUB00106643]]. Cas5 contains an endonuclease motif, whose inactivation leads to loss of resistance, even in the presence of phage-derived spacers [[cite:PUB00109113]]. This family used to be known as DUF73. DevR appears to be negative auto-regulator within the system [[cite:PUB00020781]].
family.name: CRISPR-associated negative auto-regulator DevR/Csa2

evidence.explanation: H160A retains residual binding without independent folding or bound-RNA contact evidence; cellular RNase retention lacks a matched arm isolating Csa2 protection. Cas6 cleavage is not Csa2 catalysis.

Reconstructed devT mutants revise the older distinct-role inference and support a second-site explanation for the old strain. Figure 8 is a proposed regulatory model; antisense transcript evidence is explicitly unpublished, not an observed DevTRS repression or decay mechanism.

discussions.notes: Test RNA binding and turnover with purified verified DevR/DevTRS constructs, distinguish transcription from RNA stability, measure DevI protein, and verify matched abundance/folding and allele-specific rescue. Keep suppressors distinct from DevR complementation. Do not use later review wording to promote conditional primary hypotheses to observed edges.
discussions.prompt: Resolve direct RNA contacts and the molecular basis of DevR-dependent dev RNA regulation.
discussions.rationale: Six direct binding effects and eight indirect developmental/transcript effects do not establish a continuous Csa2-to-DevR pathway, a Cas7 nuclease or direct DevR repression. The systems differ in protein, species, construct and assay.

evidence.explanation: PF01905 19-176 in the 302-aa DevR reference; exact equality with AAA16134.1/ABF86719.1/WP_011557181.1 does not independently verify the historical deletion clone or removed codons.
Hu2022 and PDB 7TR8 identify a P. furiosus Cas7a lead, but full-text access and exact construct mapping were not completed; no cleavage edge was added from the abstract.

Later Q97Y91 structures are a lead; the inspected associated manuscript metadata says To Be Published. No full paper or causal disassembly trajectory was verified, and the bounded search is not proof that no paper exists.

discussions.notes: Obtain the 2015 Table S1 and Reeks2013 supplement, verify deletion codons/catalog IDs and H160A folding/clone identity, and inspect earlier/later primary assays and archaeal members. Eight main figures and three pages of the 13-page Lintner supplement were visually inspected; no exhaustive family search, raw-data reproduction or independent scientific endorsement. Keep IN_PROGRESS.
